headline: Tideglusib delivered on a collagen sponge was reported to stimulate tooth pulp stem cells to regrow dentine
intervention: Tideglusib (GSK-3 inhibitor) on a collagen sponge
summary: King's College London researchers applied low doses of GSK-3 inhibitors, including tideglusib, to damaged teeth on biodegradable collagen sponges. The sponge degraded and was replaced by new dentine. The release gives no timeline for patient use.
article_title: Natural tooth repair method, using Alzheimer's drug, could revolutionise dental treatments

headline: A gel of calcium phosphate ion clusters was reported to grow a thin new enamel layer on damaged human teeth
summary: Zhejiang University researchers stabilised 1.5 nm calcium phosphate clusters with triethylamine in ethanol. Applied to donated human teeth, the material fused with native enamel and formed a thin repair layer. Safety tests in mice were under way.
article_title: Scientists Have Developed a Genius Method That Actually Regenerates Tooth Enamel
promise: Researchers hoped to start trials in people within one to two years

headline: Amelogenin-derived peptides were reported to rebuild a mineral layer on tooth enamel
summary: University of Washington researchers designed peptides based on amelogenin, the protein that guides enamel formation, to deposit new mineral on teeth. They proposed use in toothpaste, gels and other daily products. No clinical timeline was given.
article_title: Peptide-based biogenic dental product may cure cavities

headline: Stem cells from a child's own baby teeth were reported to regrow pulp in injured permanent teeth
intervention: Autologous dental pulp stem cells from deciduous teeth
indication: Pulp necrosis in injured immature permanent teeth
summary: A Phase I trial in China, led by the University of Pennsylvania and the Fourth Military Medical University, enrolled 40 children with an injured incisor. Those given cultured cells from their own baby teeth showed regenerated pulp and regained sensation.
article_title: Regrowing dental tissue with stem cells from baby teeth

headline: Light-curable synthetic filling materials were reported to prompt tooth stem cells to regenerate dentine
indication: Pulp and dentine damage from decay
summary: University of Nottingham and Wyss Institute researchers designed synthetic biomaterials, placed like fillings in direct contact with pulp, to stimulate native stem cells to repair pulp and dentine. The work won a Royal Society of Chemistry prize in 2016.
article_title: Fillings that heal your teeth – how regenerative medicine could change your visit to the dentist

headline: Low-dose aspirin was reported to make tooth stem cells form more dentine-like mineral in the laboratory
summary: Queen's University Belfast researchers reported that treating stem cells from teeth with low-dose aspirin increased mineralisation and dentine-forming gene expression. The stated next step was a delivery system for testing in a clinical trial.
article_title: Queen’s Research Shows Aspirin Could Repair Tooth Decay

headline: Splitting a developing tooth germ in two was reported to yield two functional teeth in mice
summary: RIKEN and Tokyo Medical and Dental University researchers partly cut mouse tooth germs with nylon thread, cultured them and implanted them in the jaw. Each germ gave two working teeth about half normal size. Suggested use: children with undeveloped teeth.
article_title: Multiplying teeth

headline: A protein-based material was reported to grow enamel-like mineral that could be used to regenerate enamel
summary: Queen Mary University of London researchers used a protein material that triggers and guides apatite nanocrystal growth into enamel-like structures. They suggested acid-resistant bandages for exposed dentine and treatment of tooth decay.
article_title: Scientists develop material that could regenerate dental enamel

headline: An injectable self-assembling peptide hydrogel was reported to stimulate dental pulp stem cells after root canal
indication: Pulp loss after root canal treatment
summary: New Jersey Institute of Technology researchers presented a peptide hydrogel, liquid when injected, meant to stimulate new blood vessels and dental pulp inside a treated tooth. Tests in dogs were under way, with human studies planned if they succeeded.
article_title: Biomaterial could keep tooth alive after root canal (video)

headline: Engineered blood vessels were reported to form inside extracted human teeth filled with a cell-laden gel
summary: OHSU researchers placed a sugar fibre mould in the root canal of extracted human teeth, injected a gel carrying dental pulp cells, then removed the fibre to leave a channel for vessel-forming cells. Vessels formed within seven days.
article_title: Study: Use of prefabricated blood vessels may revolutionize root canals

headline: Activating tooth stem cells through the Dlk1 gene was reported to enhance dentine regeneration in mice
indication: Dentine damage from decay or trauma
summary: University of Plymouth-led researchers found a new population of mesenchymal stem cells in mouse incisors that helps form dentine, and showed that Dlk1 enhances stem cell activation and tissue regeneration in tooth healing. Lab models only.
article_title: A new method of tooth repair? Scientists uncover mechanisms that could help future dental treatment

headline: A polydopamine-coated polymer membrane was reported to regenerate gum tissue and bone in periodontitis
summary: UCLA researchers built a membrane from an FDA-approved polymer with a polydopamine coating and adjustable surface patterns to promote gum tissue and bone regeneration and prolong drug delivery. It was tested in rats. No clinical timeline was given.
article_title: New class of membranes shown to regenerate tissue and bone, viable solution for periodontitis

headline: 3D bioprinting of bone, ligament and cementum was proposed to replace tissue lost around teeth
indication: Periodontal bone and gum tissue loss
summary: Griffith University researchers began a three-year, NHMRC-funded study using 3D bioprinting to make patient-specific replacement tissue for lost jaw bone and gum structures, avoiding bone grafts from elsewhere in the body. It was in pre-clinical trials.
article_title: Griffith uses 3D tissue engineering to revolutionise dental disease
promise: Aim to trial the technology in humans within the next one to two years

headline: Bioengineered tooth germs transplanted into dogs' jaws were reported to grow into functional teeth
summary: Okayama University researchers reconstructed tooth germs from a beagle's own tooth germ cells and transplanted them into its jaw, where teeth erupted. They suggested immature wisdom tooth germs as a possible cell source in people.
article_title: Okayama University Medical Research Updates （OU-MRU） Vol.38

headline: A CPNE7-derived peptide was reported to regenerate dentine as a treatment for sensitive teeth
summary: Seoul National University Dental Hospital researchers reported preclinical results in which a CPNE7 protein-based drug was absorbed through dentinal tubules and regenerated dentine, rather than blocking nerves or sealing tubules.
article_title: SNUDH to commercialize world's 1st treatment for teeth sensitive to cold
promise: Clinical trials of the peptides planned for the first half of 2020

headline: A 3D-printed bioresorbable scaffold with growth factor was used to treat a periodontal bone defect in one patient
intervention: 3D-printed bioresorbable polymer scaffold with growth factor
summary: IADR/AADR announced a Journal of Dental Research case report on the first human use of a patient-specific 3D-printed scaffold for a large periodontal bone defect. The treated site stayed intact for 12 months, then failed.
article_title: JDR articles explore 3-D printing for oral and dental tissue engineering

headline: Dental pulp stem cells delivered in a GelMA hydrogel were reported to regenerate pulp-like tissue in a rodent model
intervention: Dental pulp stem cells in GelMA hydrogel
indication: Pulp loss from decay or trauma
summary: Tufts researchers encapsulated human dental pulp stem cells and endothelial cells in gelatin methacrylate and delivered them into tooth root segments tested in a rodent model. Pulp-like tissue formed. They called for larger animal studies before human trials.
article_title: New stem cell delivery approach regenerates dental pulp-like tissue in a rodent model

headline: Donor fat-derived stem cells were reported to regenerate periodontal tissue in minipigs
summary: Tohoku University-led researchers transplanted adipose-derived multi-lineage progenitor cells from donor animals into a minipig periodontal defect model and reported tissue regeneration. They said they planned a clinical trial; no date was given.
article_title: Promising Treatment for Periodontitis Gum Regeneration

headline: Maresin-1 and Resolvin E1 were reported to restore the regenerative capacity of tooth stem cells under inflammation
summary: Forsyth Institute scientists took stem cells from extracted wisdom teeth, simulated periodontal inflammation in a dish and added the lipid mediators Maresin-1 and Resolvin E1, which stimulated the cells to regenerate. Laboratory study only.
article_title: Forsyth researchers demonstrate how changing the stem cell response to inflammation may reverse periodontal disease

headline: A shortened amelogenin-based peptide was reported to grow a harder enamel-like layer on softened enamel
summary: USC researchers engineered a short peptide containing only the parts of amelogenin needed for enamel crystal formation. Over seven days it grew an enamel-like layer twice as hard as softened control enamel. The article says clinical trials are years away.
outlet: Herman Ostrow School of Dentistry of USC
article_title: Ostrow Researcher Makes Strides in Gel to Regrow Tooth Enamel

headline: The adiponectin-mimicking compound AdipoRon was proposed to rebuild jaw bone lost to diabetic gum disease
summary: A Tufts dental school lab was studying AdipoRon, an experimental compound that mimics the hormone adiponectin, as a way to rebuild bone in hard-to-treat periodontal disease in people with type 2 diabetes. Dose and mechanism were still unclear.
article_title: New experimental drug promises hope for those with diabetic periodontal disease

headline: Tooth germs grown from a patient's own dental pulp cells were proposed as a way to regrow teeth
intervention: Tooth germ from autologous dental pulp cells
summary: TU Berlin researchers reported coaxing cells from extracted teeth to condense into an embryonic-like tooth germ, intended for implantation in the jaw to grow a new tooth. In-vitro tests were complete and pre-clinical tests were next.
article_title: Regrowing Teeth

headline: A polymer membrane with zinc oxide nanoparticles was developed to fight periodontitis and aid bone regeneration
summary: A University of Nebraska-Lincoln-led team developed a membrane containing zinc oxide, chosen to prevent bacterial growth and aid bone regeneration while keeping gum tissue out of the defect. Finding the right zinc oxide concentration was still open.
article_title: Research team aims to develop periodontal disease-fighting membrane
